newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's key rate seen falling to 5 pct by mid-June.
newsitem.headline: Spain's key rate seen falling to 5 pct by mid-June.

text.p: Spain's key money market rate is likely to be trimmed by a further 50 basis points to five percent in the next two months, a Morgan Stanley study said.

The report projects further monetary easing based on the expectation that the inflation rate will drop to 1.8 percent in April and to 1.7 percent in May, thanks partly to basis effects, given last year's rise in the food prices.
Spain's consumer price index rose 2.2 percent year-on-year in March, down from February's 2.5 percent.
"Because the expected drop in inflation should occur in the next two months ...we believe it makes sense to expect up to two 25-basis-point cuts by the Bank of Spain," the report writes.
The Bank of Spain, which has cut its key money market rate three times so far this year. The last cut was on April 16 after release of the March CPI figure.
Currently, Spain's official rate stands at 5.50 percent.

Morgan Stanley said the overall decline in Bank of Spain intervention rate in the last six months had been higher than it expected because "the inflation rate had surprised on the downside, falling 70 basis points more than expected".
"By June, when the May inflation data are released, the intervention rate would be down to 5 percent," the report said.
